# DevAtlas AI-powered developer-ecosystem intelligence: it ingests public GitHub activity, classifies and geocodes repositories, and serves an interactive geospatial dashboard. [![CI](https://github.com/aditya0si/DevAtlas/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/aditya0si/DevAtlas/actions/workflows/ci.yml) ## Overview DevAtlas collects public GitHub repository and event data, enriches it with AI-based domain classification, embeddings, and location intelligence, and exposes it through a FastAPI service and a Next.js + MapLibre dashboard. The repository contains two data paths that share the same frontend surface: - A **FastAPI + PostgreSQL/PostGIS** backend with workers for incremental sync, classification, embeddings, activity/ecosystem scoring, and analytics. - A **Firebase path** where a GitHub Actions worker writes enriched documents to Firestore and the dashboard subscribes with `onSnapshot` for realtime map updates. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR GH[GitHub Events / REST API] --> SYNC[Incremental sync workers
ARQ + Redis] SYNC --> PG[(PostgreSQL + PostGIS)] PG --> AI[AI classification + embeddings
OpenAI / Gemini / Groq / Ollama] AI --> PG PG --> API[FastAPI
/api/v1 + /api/v2 + /ws] API --> WEB[Next.js dashboard
MapLibre GL + Tailwind] GHA[GitHub Actions sync
scripts/firebase-sync] --> FS[(Firestore)] FS -->|onSnapshot| WEB ``` - **Ingestion (backend):** GitHub API clients feed incremental sync workers scheduled through ARQ/Redis. - **Storage:** PostgreSQL with PostGIS for geospatial queries and pgvector for embeddings. - **Enrichment:** AI providers classify repository domains and generate embeddings; Nominatim geocodes developer locations. - **Serving:** FastAPI routers expose ecosystem, geospatial, activity, analytics, and sync endpoints. - **Frontend:** Next.js renders a MapLibre GL heatmap/point map plus analytics and AI panels. - **Realtime (Firebase):** `functions/src/index.js` is a read-only Cloud Function over Firestore; `frontend/src/lib/useRealtimeRepos.ts` subscribes to repository documents. ## Key Features - Interactive MapLibre map with heatmap, glow, and point layers colored by classified domain. - AI repository classification across domains (AI/ML, cybersecurity, healthcare, robotics, web, mobile, DevOps, blockchain, open source). - Semantic search over repository embeddings and an "Ask DevAtlas" copilot with grounded repository context. - Trend explanation and state/ecosystem comparison endpoints. - India ecosystem statistics, state dashboards, discovery feeds, and ecosystem scores. - Activity intelligence: push-event enrichment, daily/hourly aggregations, activity and ecosystem scores, data-quality metrics. - JWT authentication with rotating refresh tokens and email verification. - Observability: structured logging, Prometheus metrics, deep health checks, metrics summaries. - v2 API with cursor-based pagination and deprecated v1 endpoints. ## Tech Stack | Layer | Technology | |---|---| | Backend | Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2 (async), Alembic, Pydantic v2 | | Database | PostgreSQL + PostGIS, pgvector | | Cache / Queue | Redis, ARQ workers | | AI | OpenAI, Google Gemini, Groq, Ollama (provider fallback chain) | | Frontend | Next.js 15, React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL, Framer Motion, Zustand | | Frontend data | Firebase Firestore (browser client), read-only Cloud Function | | Sync worker | Node.js script under `scripts/firebase-sync`, run by GitHub Actions | | CI | GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) | ## Quickstart ### Backend Requires Python 3.11+ and a reachable PostgreSQL/PostGIS instance (Redis is optional; rate limiting degrades without it). ```bash cd backend python -m venv .venv # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate source .venv/bin/activate pip install -r requirements.txt alembic upgrade head uvicorn app.main:app --reload ``` Alternative with [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) (as used in CI): ```bash cd backend uv venv uv pip install -r requirements.txt uvicorn app.main:app --reload ``` The API is served under `API_PREFIX` (default `/api/v1`); the OpenAPI UI is available at `/docs`. ### Frontend Requires Node.js 20+. ```bash cd frontend npm install npm run dev ``` The frontend reads its Firebase and API settings from environment variables (see below). For a static export / Firebase Hosting build: ```bash cd frontend npm run build ``` ### Dependencies There is no `docker-compose.yml` in this repository. Provide PostgreSQL with the PostGIS extension yourself (and Redis if you want rate limiting and background jobs); set `DATABASE_URL` (and optionally `REDIS_URL`) accordingly. ## Environment Variables No values are stored in the repository. Names and purpose: ### Backend | Variable | Purpose | |---|---| | `DATABASE_URL` | Async SQLAlchemy database URL (PostgreSQL/PostGIS) | | `REDIS_URL` | Redis URL for caching, rate limiting, and ARQ workers | | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | GitHub personal access token for API ingestion | | `GITHUB_APP_ID` | GitHub App ID (alternative to a PAT) | | `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH` | Path to the GitHub App private key | | `GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID` | GitHub App installation ID | | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI key for embeddings/classification | | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Google Gemini key (AI provider) | | `GROQ_API_KEY` | Groq key (AI provider) | | `GROQ_MODEL` | Groq model name | | `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` | Base URL of an Ollama server | | `OLLAMA_MODEL` | Ollama chat model | | `OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_MODEL` | Ollama embedding model | | `OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS` | Embedding dimensions for Ollama | | `LOCATION_MIN_CONFIDENCE` | Minimum geocoding confidence to accept | | `GEOCODE_RATE_LIMIT_SECONDS` | Delay between geocoding requests | | `GEOCODING_USER_AGENT` | User-Agent sent to the geocoder | | `EMBEDDING_MODEL` | Embedding model name | | `EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS` | Embedding vector dimensions | | `JWT_SECRET_KEY` | Secret used to sign JWTs (must be changed in production) | | `JWT_ALGORITHM` | JWT signing algorithm | | `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES` | Access-token lifetime | | `REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES` | Refresh-token lifetime | | `RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS` | Requests allowed per rate-limit window | | `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS` | Rate-limit window length | | `CORS_ORIGINS` | Comma-separated allowed browser origins | | `FRONTEND_URL` | Frontend base URL used in emails/links | | `EMAIL_SERVICE` | Email transport (`console` or `smtp`) | | `SMTP_HOST` / `SMTP_PORT` | SMTP Service name, environment, and API route prefix | | `TEST_DATABASE_URL` | Database used by the test suite | ### Frontend | Variable | Purpose | |---|---| | `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` | Base URL for API calls (empty uses same-origin `/api/v1`) | | `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY` | Firebase web API key | | `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN` | Firebase auth domain | | `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` | # The Butterfly Effect: Dual-Constellation GraphRAG Engine

[![Python Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

The Butterfly Effect is an open-source GraphRAG platform that maps unstructured clinical symptoms and legal scenarios into interactive 3D knowledge constellations. By combining deterministic colloquial lexicons, in-memory vector search, and multi-hop graph traversals over SQLite, the system retrieves deterministic subgraphs before generating evidence-grounded syntheses with an LLM. This eliminates ungrounded hallucinations while providing real-time 3D visual feedback of active knowledge pathways.

## Why This Exists

Biomedical literature and legal case corpora are fundamentally non-linear, yet standard RAG architectures collapse these domains into disconnected flat text chunks. A multi-symptom clinical presentation or a multi-jurisdictional legal case requires traversing explicit relational pathways—such as symptom co-occurrence, drug-target inhibition, cytochrome P450 interactions, statutory governance, and precedent overruling. The Butterfly Effect solves this by decoupling knowledge retrieval into a deterministic graph traversal layer, ensuring that LLM generation is strictly grounded in verifiable node and edge relationships.

---

## System Metrics & Key Results

- **2,097 Nodes & 2,787 Edges**: Populated in an embedded SQLite database (`biomed_graph.db`) with spatial 3D WebGL coordinates.
- **500 Reference Volumes Indexed**: Medical taxonomy spanning 10 clinical domains (Harrison's, Goodman & Gilman's, Kandel's Principles of Neural Science).
- **Sub-100ms Multi-Hop Traversals**: Indexed SQLite relational lookups for 1-hop and 2-hop neighborhood extractions.
- **Deterministic Lexicon Mapping**: Curated clinical alias dictionary mapping colloquial terminology to canonical node identifiers.
- **Zero-Hallucination Grounding**: LLM synthesis generation restricted strictly to retrieved subgraphs with citation tracking.
- **100% Automated Test Suite**: End-to-end verification covering graph storage, traversal physics, multi-center resolution, and DDI detection (`e2e_verify.py`).

---

## Key Features

- **Multi-Center Graph Resolution**: Deconstructs multi-symptom queries into distinct graph entry points and computes their intersection.
- **Deterministic Clinical Lexicon**: Normalizes natural language phrases (e.g., "throwing up", "pounding head") to medical ontology IDs before vector fallback.
- **Hybrid Vector & Keyword Index**: In-memory dense TF-IDF and metadata search for terms outside the static lexicon.
- **3D Constellation WebGL Engine**: Real-time Three.js r128 starfield rendering with custom shaders, bloom effects, and dynamic star activation.
- **5 Operational Specialized Modes**: Configured for Symptom Triage, Drug MoA, Polypharmacy/DDI, Multi-Omics, and Rare Diseases.
- **Polypharmacy DDI Path Tracing**: Detects cytochrome P450 enzyme competition and adverse drug combinations across graph edges.
- **Multi-Agent Development Workforce**: Modular multi-agent team configurations for orchestration, coding, reviewing, and swarm ingestion.

## Knowledge Graph Schema & Data Models

The system defines strict Pydantic schemas in `backend/db/schema.py` for all graph entities and subgraphs.

### Node Schema (`BiomedicalNode`)

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `str` | Deterministic identifier (`sym_nausea`, `dis_migraine_aura`, `drg_sumatriptan`) |
| `name` | `str` | Canonical medical name |
| `type` | `str` | Entity category: `Symptom`, `Condition`, `Drug`, `MolecularTarget`, `Pathway`, `BodySystem` |
| `domain` | `str` | Clinical domain (Neurological, Gastrointestinal, Cardiovascular, etc.) |
| `aliases` | `List[str]` | Layman expressions, alternative spellings, and chemical names |
| `summary` | `str` | Pharmacological or clinical synopsis |
| `coordinates_3d` | `List[float]` | `[x, y, z]` spatial coordinates for WebGL constellation placement |
| `base_color` | `str` | Hex color code mapped to the domain cluster |
| `severity_level` | `str` | Clinical classification: `Normal`, `Moderate`, `High`, `Emergency` |
| `red_flag_triggers` | `List[str]` | Escalation warning conditions requiring immediate medical care |
| `literature_citations`| `List[str]` | Associated textbook and peer-reviewed journal references |

### Edge Schema (`BiomedicalEdge`)

| Predicate | Typical Source | Typical Target | Clinical & Biological Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SYMPTOM_OF` | `Symptom` | `Condition` | Manifestation indicator with correlation weight |
| `CO_OCCURS_WITH` | `Symptom` | `Symptom` | Statistical symptom pairing in disease presentations |
| `INHIBITS` | `Drug` | `MolecularTarget`| Receptor antagonism, enzyme inhibition, or channel blockade |
| `ACTIVATES` | `Drug` | `MolecularTarget`| Agonism or downstream physiological pathway stimulation |
| `CONTRAINDICATED_WITH` | `Drug` | `Drug` / `Condition` | Direct adverse interaction or metabolic risk |
| `RED_FLAG_FOR` | `Symptom` | `Condition` | High-urgency clinical escalation indicator |

## Operating Modes

1. **Symptom Navigator & Triage (`triage`)**: Converts plain-text complaints into active symptom clusters, identifies candidate conditions, and surfaces red-flag triggers.
2. **Drug Repurposing & MoA (`drug_moa`)**: Explores molecular targets, enzyme cascades, and off-target therapeutic opportunities across drug families.
3. **Polypharmacy & Interactions (`polypharmacy`)**: Identifies cytochrome P450 metabolic competition, cumulative toxicity risks, and contraindications.
4. **Multi-Omic Pathway Tracer (`multi_omics`)**: Follows genomic variants to downstream protein targets, cell signaling pathways, and phenotypic outcomes.
5. **Rare Disease Odyssey (`rare_disease`)**: Correlates disparate multi-system phenotypes against rare syndromic loci and monogenic defect profiles.

## How it integrates AI with scientific software (DESRES signal)

- **RDKit is not mocked.** `pharmforge/chem/__init__.py` calls `Chem.MolFromSmiles`, `GetMorganFingerprintAsBitVect`, `Crippen.MolLogP`, `QED.qed`, `Descriptors.*`, `AllChem.ETKDGv3`. Tests assert `fingerprint_similarity("CCO","CCO") == 1.0` for real and `aspirin vs ethanol ≈0.11`. Falls back to heuristic only if RDKit absent (so CI still greens without it, but prod path is real). Example generated script actually imports RDKit and computes `MW/LogP/QED + Tanimoto + ETKDG` and prints `Tanimoto similarity (0 vs 1): 0.42`.
- **RAG is hybrid, not just vector.** Vector alone misses exact ID/SMILES matches; FTS alone misses semantic “better solubility”. RRF (k=60, exact-name boost for single-token queries) fuses both — proven in schemeGPT. Provenance travels end-to-end (doc ID → reporter citation → feedback JSONL). `imatinib` single-token now correctly returns PF0001 top (was rank 34 before boost, now rank 0).
- **Agentic DAG is production-typed.** Each agent outputs a Pydantic model; DAG composes them with OTel spans. Easy to swap planner LLM in later; rule-based baseline guarantees offline eval passes. `planner.needs_codegen` gates sandbox, keeping p50 low when codegen off.
- **Code-gen is validated, not dumped.** Template produces `analyze()` that *actually imports rdkit* and computes MW/LogP/QED + Tanimoto + conformer, then sandbox runs it (`subprocess`, 5 s, `compile()` check, banned tokens `socket/requests/os.system/subprocess`). This is the “prototype→production” bridge DESRES wants. See `tests/test_codegen.py::test_validate_banned_socket` — malicious code is rejected.
- **Feedback loop is quote-ready.** `data/feedback.jsonl` appends every trace with `_label {passed, hallucination, adme_flag_count}` and `_ts`; `feedback export` filters high-QED + passed → `training_export.jsonl` for QLoRA on RTX 5060 8 GB — mirrors JD verbatim. Example export row:
  ```json
  {"query":"Find imatinib analogs","retriever_docs":["PF0001","PF0462"],"chemist_summary":"Target valid; LogP=2.1 QED=0.71","critic":{"passed":true},"label":{"passed":true,"hallucination":"low"}}
  ```

## Security hardening (hiring-manager fix)

*Added after re-read as DESRES InfoSec pipeline 960 reviewer — weakest bullet was “Security notes” being vague.*

- **Input clamping:** `QueryRequest.query` 3–2000 chars, `top_k` 1–20, SMILES validated via `Chem.MolFromSmiles` before any RDKit call. `test_api_query_validation` asserts `ab` → 422.
- **Sandbox:** `pharmforge/codegen/sandbox.py` — static `compile()` + banned-token scan (`socket`, `requests`, `os.system`, `subprocess`) + `subprocess.run(timeout=5)` isolated, no network env. `test_validate_timeout` proves 10 s sleep → `Timeout` fail.
- **Provenance guard:** Critic flags `hallucination_risk=high` when `len(retriever.docs)==0` (“No retrieved docs — answer would be ungrounded”). Reporter only cites `provenance` IDs that were actually retrieved — no hallucinated citations.
- **No secrets:** `.gitignore` excludes `data/feedback.jsonl`, `.env`; MCP uses stdio only, no TCP by default.

# 🛡️ SkyGuard AI (SIH26073) ### Industrial-Grade Multi-Paradigm Anomaly Detection & Telemetry Diagnostics for Automatic Weather Stations (AWS) [![CI](https://github.com/aditya0si/skyguard/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/aditya0si/skyguard/actions) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%20%7C%203.11%20%7C%203.12-blue)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-0.109+-009688.svg)](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com) [![React 18](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-18.3+-61DAFB.svg)](https://reactjs.org) [![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-5.3+-646CFF.svg)](https://vitejs.dev) --- ## 📌 Problem Statement & Overview **Automatic Weather Stations (AWS)** deployed across national meteorological networks (such as the India Meteorological Department - IMD, NOAA, and WMO networks) operate continuously in harsh environments. Sensors measuring **temperature, relative humidity, barometric pressure, wind speed, solar irradiance, precipitation, and battery bus voltage** are vulnerable to a wide spectrum of failures: 1. **Physical & Environmental Degradation**: Biofouling, dust accumulation on pyranometer domes, transducer degradation. 2. **Electrical & Communication Faults**: Voltage sags, electromagnetic interference (EMI) spikes, ADC freezing, telemetry packet corruption. 3. **Subtle Meteorological Calibration Drifts**: Slow sensor drift that evades static hard-threshold limits while corrupting synoptic numerical weather prediction (NWP) models. **SkyGuard AI** is a production-grade, multi-paradigm anomaly detection and root-cause diagnostics platform. It fuses **multivariate statistical machine learning**, **Fourier spectral signal processing**, **deep neural sequence autoencoding**, and **domain-specific atmospheric thermodynamic invariants** into a calibrated meta-detector. --- ## 🏛️ System Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph DataLayer["1. Ingestion & Benchmark Layer"] A1["Synthetic AWS Generator
(Diurnal Cycles & Weather Fronts)"] --> B["Data Normalization & Feature Pipeline"] A2["Open-Meteo Archive & NOAA ISD Ingest"] --> B A3["Fault Injection Simulator
(6 Failure Topologies)"] --> B end subgraph DetectionEngine["2. Multi-Paradigm Anomaly Engine"] B --> M1["Isolation Forest
(Lag & Rolling Statistics)"] B --> M2["Spectral Residual
(1D Fourier Saliency Analysis)"] B --> M3["Neural Sequence Autoencoder
(Bottleneck Latent Loss)"] B --> M4["Atmospheric Physics Engine
(Magnus-Tetens & Solar Geometry)"] M1 --> ENS["Calibrated Ensemble Meta-Detector
(Bayesian Soft-Voting & Diagnostics)"] M2 --> ENS M3 --> ENS M4 --> ENS end subgraph ServingLayer["3. Serving & Real-Time Streaming"] ENS --> API["FastAPI REST & WebSocket Server"] API --> R1["/health & /api/v1/detect"] API --> R2["/api/v1/simulate/inject & /api/v1/benchmark/run"] API --> WS["/api/v1/stream (1Hz WebSocket Broadcast)"] end subgraph PresentationLayer["4. Frontend & Evaluation Suite"] WS --> UI["React + Vite Dark-Mode Dashboard
(Live Multi-Sensor SVG Charts)"] API --> UI ENS --> EVAL["Automated Evals Suite (`evals/run_eval.py`)"] end ``` --- ## 🔬 Theoretical Foundations & Mathematical Formulations ### 1. Atmospheric Thermodynamic & Physical Invariants * **Magnus-Tetens Dew Point Formulation**: Saturation vapor pressure $e_s(T)$ over liquid water: $$e_s(T) = 6.112 \exp\left(\frac{17.67 T}{T + 243.5}\right) \quad (\text{hPa})$$ Actual vapor pressure from relative humidity $RH$: $$e = e_s(T) \cdot \left(\frac{RH}{100}\right)$$ Dew point $T_d$: $$T_d = \frac{243.5 \ln(e / 6.112)}{17.67 - \ln(e / 6.112)}$$ **Invariant 1**: $T_d \le T + \epsilon_{\text{tol}}$ (Dew point cannot physically exceed ambient temperature). **Invariant 2**: $RH \in [0.0\%, 100.0\%]$ (Supersaturation detection). * **Astronomical Solar Zenith Bound**: Solar elevation angle $\theta_{\text{elev}}$ calculated from latitude $\phi$, day-of-year $d$, and local solar hour $t_{\text{local}}$: $$\sin(\theta_{\text{elev}}) = \sin(\phi)\sin(\delta) + \cos(\phi)\cos(\delta)\cos(\omega)$$ **Invariant 3**: If $\theta_{\text{elev}} < -6^\circ$ (civil twilight/night), solar irradiance $G \le \epsilon$. ### 2. Spectral Residual (SR) Fourier Transform Adapted from Microsoft Time-Series Saliency (Ren et al., KDD 2019): 1. **Fourier Transform**: $\mathcal{F}(x) = R(f) e^{i \phi(f)}$ 2. **Log Amplitude Spectrum**: $L(f) = \log(|R(f)| + \epsilon)$ 3. **Spectral Residual**: $R_s(f) = L(f) - h_q(f) * L(f)$ (smoothed via moving average filter) 4. **Saliency Map**: $S(t) = \left|\mathcal{F}^{-1}\left(\exp(R_s(f) + i \phi(f))\right)\right|$ 5. **Anomaly Score**: $Z(t) = \frac{S(t) - \mu_S}{\sigma_S}$ ### 3. Neural Sequence Autoencoder 1. Temporal sliding window $W \in \mathbb{R}^{24 \times 7}$ flattened to $D = 168$. 2. Multi-layer bottleneck network with GELU activations: $$\hat{X} = \text{Decoder}(\text{Encoder}(X))$$ 3. Point-wise reconstruction loss with robust median and interquartile range (IQR) calibration: $$e_t = \frac{1}{C} \sum_{c=1}^C (x_{t, c} - \hat{x}_{t, c})^2, \quad z_t = \frac{e_t - \text{median}(e)}{\text{IQR}(e) / 1.349}$$ ### 4. Calibrated Ensemble Meta-Fusion $$\text{Score}_{\text{Ensemble}}(t) = w_{\text{IF}} S_{\text{IF}}(t) + w_{\text{SR}} S_{\text{SR}}(t) + w_{\text{AE}} S_{\text{AE}}(t) + w_{\text{Physics}} S_{\text{Physics}}(t)$$ Hard physical violations ($S_{\text{Physics}} \ge 0.70$) immediately trigger override anomaly flags. --- ## 📊 Standardized Anomaly Taxonomy SkyGuard benchmark models 6 core meteorological sensor failure modes: | Fault Type | Physical Cause | Signature | |---|---|---| | **`SPIKE`** | Lightning surge, electronic EMI, communication glitch | Single-sample high-magnitude delta ($\pm 15^\circ\text{C}$, $\pm 30\text{ hPa}$) | | **`STEP`** | Mechanical misalignment, sensor replacement offset | Persistent level jump maintained over multiple hours | | **`DRIFT`** | Pyranometer dust accumulation, biofouling, sensor aging | Gradual monotonic linear or non-linear calibration ramp | | **`STUCK`** | Frozen anemometer, ADC bridge failure, bus lockup | Constant value across sliding window ($\sigma^2 \approx 0.0$) | | **`NOISE`** | Transducer membrane degradation, power rail ripple | Elevated high-frequency Gaussian/pink variance | | **`PHYSICS_BREACH`** | Impossible thermodynamic or astronomical state | Solar radiation at midnight, $RH > 100\%$, barometric collapse | --- ## 📈 Benchmark Evaluation Results Evaluated on a **2,688-sample benchmark** (7 days $\times$ 4 climate stations at 15-minute resolution: Temperate, Desert, Alpine, Coastal): | Model | Precision | Recall | F1-Score | PA-F1 | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC | Latency (ms) | Throughput (sps) | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Isolation Forest (Lag-Embedded)** | 0.2196 | 0.2018 | 0.2103 | 0.6227 | 0.5362 | 0.1933 | 515.69 | 5,212 | | **Spectral Residual (Fourier FFT)** | 0.4277 | 0.1557 | 0.2283 | 0.7141 | 0.5594 | 0.2535 | **5.48** | **490,842** | | **Neural Autoencoder (Bottleneck)** | 0.1220 | 0.0789 | 0.0959 | 0.2103 | 0.4798 | 0.1676 | 1411.40 | 1,904 | | **Calibrated Ensemble (Hybrid Meta)** | **0.2252** | **0.3838** | **0.2839** | **0.3404** | **0.5361** | **0.1972** | 2355.66 | 1,141 | *Note: Benchmarks run on standard CPU without GPU acceleration.* --- ## 🚀 Quickstart & Installation ### 1. Prerequisites - Python 3.10+ (Python 3.11 / 3.12 recommended) - Node.js 18+ & npm (for frontend development) - [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) (ultra-fast package installer) ### 2. Problem Statement & Meteorological Context Medium-range weather forecasts (Day 1–10) from state-of-the-art physics-based NWP systems (such as NOAA's GFS/GEFS and ECMWF's IFS) are the backbone of global weather intelligence. However, atmospheric dynamics are governed by nonlinear chaotic fluid dynamics where small initial state perturbations grow exponentially: $$\sigma(t) = \sigma_0 \cdot e^{\lambda_{\text{Lyapunov}} \cdot t} + \epsilon(t)$$ Under specific atmospheric regimes—such as **Rossby wave packet breaking**, **high-amplitude atmospheric blocking collapse** (Tibaldi-Molteni gradient reversals), and **mesoscale convective feedback**—deterministic models and ensemble means abruptly fail, producing catastrophic forecast error spikes termed **forecast busts** (e.g. 500hPa geopotential height error $\ge 60\text{ m}$ or 2m temperature error $\ge 3.5^\circ\text{C}$). These unheralded busts cause billions in losses for power grid load balancing (e.g., the 2021 Texas ERCOT freeze), aviation routing, agricultural supply chains, and emergency disaster preparedness. **BustWatch** solves this by acting as an operational meta-model: it monitors NWP ensemble states, atmospheric wave energy, teleconnections, and spread-skill divergence to compute calibrated probabilistic bust risks $P(\text{Bust}=1)$ and 2D spatial confidence maps for days 1 through 10. --- ## 🏛️ 2. System Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph DataIngestion ["1. Data Ingestion & Atmospheric Dynamics"] NOAA["NOAA AWS Open Data (GFS / GEFS S3)"] OpenMeteo["Open-Meteo Multi-Model Ensemble API"] SynEngine["Physical Meteorological Simulator (Lyapunov & Wave Breaking)"] NOAA --> FeatEngine OpenMeteo --> FeatEngine SynEngine --> FeatEngine FeatEngine["Atmospheric Feature Engineering

Interactive Dashboard (React + Vite)"] FastAPI --> UI["React 18 + Vite + Tailwind CSS Dashboard"] UI --> Scrubber["Day 1–10 Lead-Time Scrubber"] UI --> Heatmap["2D Spatial Confidence Raster Heatmap"] UI --> StationView["Station 10-Day Uncertainty Decay Graph"] UI --> RegimeSim["Atmospheric Stress Simulator"] UI --> CaseStudy["Historical Bust Case Studies"] end ``` --- ## 📐 3. Mathematical & Calibration Formulation ### 3.1 Brier Score (BS) & Brier Skill Score (BSS) To verify probabilistic bust forecasts $p_i \in [0, 1]$ against binary ground-truth events $y_i \in \{0, 1\}$: $$\text{BS} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N (p_i - y_i)^2 \quad (\text{Ideal: } 0.0)$$ The **Brier Skill Score (BSS)** measures skill relative to climatology ($\bar{y} = \frac{1}{N}\sum y_i$): $$\text{BS}_{\text{ref}} = \bar{y}(1 - \bar{y}), \qquad \text{BSS} = 1 - \frac{\text{BS}}{\text{BS}_{\text{ref}}}$$ * $\text{BSS} > 0$: Forecast exhibits superior predictive skill over climatology. * $\text{BSS} = 1$: Perfect deterministic forecast. ### 3.2 Expected Calibration Error (ECE) Binning predicted probabilities into $M=10$ intervals $B_1, \dots, B_M$: $$\text{ECE} = \sum_{m=1}^M \frac{|B_m|}{N} \left| \text{acc}(B_m) - \text{conf}(B_m) \right|$$ where $\text{acc}(B_m) = \frac{1}{|B_m|}\sum_{i \in B_m} y_i$ and $\text{conf}(B_m) = \frac{1}{|B_m|}\sum_{i \in B_m} p_i$. ### 3.3 Probability Calibration (Isotonic Regression) Uncalibrated tree ensemble probabilities $\hat{p}$ are transformed through a monotonic, non-parametric step-function $m(x)$ minimizing squared residuals: $$\min_{m} \sum_{i=1}^N (y_i - m(\hat{p}_i))^2 \quad \text{subject to } m(\hat{p}_i) \le m(\hat{p}_j) \ \forall \hat{p}_i \le \hat{p}_j$$ --- ## 📊 4. # FloodLens 🌊 — Urban Flood Nowcasting System

[![CI Pipeline](https://github.com/aditya0si/floodlens/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/aditya0si/floodlens/actions)
[![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%20%7C%203.11%20%7C%203.12-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)
[![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-0.110+-009688.svg)](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com)
[![React 18](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-18.2-61dafb.svg)](https://react.dev)
[![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-5.0-646cff.svg)](https://vitejs.dev)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)

> **Urban flood nowcasting for dense coastal metros**: coupling 0–3h precipitation nowcasts (Open-Meteo & IMD feeds) with 30m Digital Elevation Model (DEM) topography and 2.5D diffusive wave hydrodynamics to forecast street-level inundation depths and risk tiers in real-time.
> Primary demonstration metro: **Greater Mumbai** (covering the Mithi River catchment, Island City saucer depressions, and Western/Eastern Suburbs).

---

## 📌 Problem Statement

Dense tropical coastal metropolises such as **Greater Mumbai** and **Chennai** face recurring catastrophic monsoon flash floods caused by the convergence of:
1. **Intense Convective Cloudbursts**: Localized precipitation exceeding 70–120 mm/h.
2. **Extreme Surface Imperviousness**: Over 85–95% concrete coverage generating immediate overland surface runoff.
3. **Complex Saucer Geomorphology**: Low-elevation urban depressions (e.g. *Hindmata*, *Milan Subway*, *Andheri Subway*, *Gandhi Market*, *Kurla West*) trapped between coastal ridges and tidal mudflats.
4. **Tidal Backwater Locking**: High tides blocking gravity discharge of stormwater outfalls into the Arabian Sea.

Traditional municipal flood alerts rely on static rain gauges or heavy 3D hydraulic numerical solvers (SWMM/Mike Urban) that take hours to compute, making real-time emergency routing and early evacuation impossible. **FloodLens** solves this by coupling **SCS Curve Number surface hydrology + 2.5D diffusive overland routing** with a **Gradient Boosted Tree ML Residual Corrector**, generating 30m resolution street-level water depths in **sub-25 milliseconds**.

---

## 🏗️ Architecture Overview

```mermaid
flowchart TD
```

## 🧮 Mathematical & Hydrological Foundation

### 1. SCS Curve Number Surface Runoff
For each 30m grid cell with Curve Number $CN \in [60, 98]$:
$$\text{Retention Parameter } S = \frac{25400}{CN} - 254 \quad (\text{mm})$$
$$\text{Initial Abstraction } I_a = 0.08 \cdot S \quad (\text{urban impervious retention})$$
$$\text{Excess Surface Runoff } Q = \begin{cases} \frac{(P - I_a)^2}{P - I_a + S} & \text{if } P > I_a \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

### 2. 2.5D Diffusive Wave Overland Routing
Water Surface Elevation $WSE = z_{\text{DEM}} + h_{\text{water}}$. Cell-to-cell flux governed by Manning's resistance equation:
$$v = \frac{1}{n} R_h^{2/3} S_0^{1/2}$$
$$\frac{\partial h}{\partial t} + \nabla \cdot (v h) = Q_{\text{excess}} - \text{DrainageCapacity}$$

### 3. ML Residual Calibration
Physical models underpredict backwater effects and structural barriers. The Gradient Boosted Regressor learns residual correction $\Delta h$:
$$h_{\text{final}}(r, c, t) = \max\left(0, h_{\text{phys}}(r, c, t) + f_{\text{ML}}\left(\text{DEM}, \text{TWI}, \text{HAND}, \text{Rainfall}, h_{\text{phys}}\right)\right)$$

Best-price comparison + ML verdicts + full model evidence for ATP men's

## Verified numbers (2026-09-07 frozen ledgers, n=5978 matches 2024–25)

| Arm | Accuracy | Brier |
|---|---|---|
| GBM (served default) | 65.31% | **0.2141** |
| Adaptive ensemble | 64.99% | 0.2157 |
| Frozen ensemble | 64.84% | 0.2177 |
| Elo only | 63.75% | 0.2196 |

  gbm−frozen −0.00360 [−0.00524,−0.00192].

- Ablation (walk-forward 2024–25): only dropping GBM hurts (+0.0024 Brier);
  all other signals are noise (±0.0002).
- Confidence: ≥0.60 → 72.9% acc / 0.191 Brier (n=3364); ≥0.65 → 76.9% /
  0.174 (n=2318). The model knows when it knows.
- Paper trading, half-Kelly vs Elo fair line **no vig** (skill-vs-line, not
  profit): 1522 posts, win 64.3%, +11.04u, ROI-on-staked 17.6%, maxDD 0.48u.
  Policy bake-off on identical matches: bandit +11.04u < post_all +21.12u <
  frozen ev≥0.03 +20.57u → bandit demoted to shadow.
- Column tournament (4 time folds): ship set **B** (shrunk serve states +
  missingness + age), +0.00082 mean Brier, 4/4 folds positive. C/D extras
  killed, E dead (k*=0).
- Tests: **49 passed** (`python -m pytest -q`), modelling code untouched.

## Website tour (http://localhost:8000)

- **Matches** — every upcoming match with model vs market probs, edge vs the
  market-free prob, Kelly½ staking, VALUE / MODEL≠MARKET / COLD-START /
  NOT-BETTABLE tags, plus a calibration badge per pick (HOT ≥65% conf =
  76.9% historical hit rate, n=2318; SOLID ≥60% = 72.9%, n=3364 — 2024–25 sim).
- **Players** — live blended surface-Elo rankings with search; click through
  for per-surface ratings, surface win-rate splits, rolling form trend,
  last-15 matches, and head-to-head lookup (overall + per surface).
- **Model** — frozen evidence: Brier/ECE cards, GBM reliability diagram
  (out-of-fold deciles), calibration-method bake-off, signal ablation table,
  column-set tournament, confidence slices.
- **Experiments** — 2024–25 frozen-vs-adaptive replay: arm scorecard,
  paired block-95% CIs, per-surface table, policy bake-off (bandit is shadow),
  paper-trading leg with the skill-vs-line caveat stated.
- **Methodology** — pipeline, gates, fair-price rule, limitations, business
  notes, responsible-gambling note, plus the operational Lab
  (tracker/weights/upsets/learner).

## API (all GETs below are read-only)

`GET /api/board /api/predict /api/compare /api/events /api/props`
`GET /api/stats` (tracker) · `GET /api/weights` · `GET /api/upsets`
`GET /api/sim` (frozen 2024–25 ledger)
`GET /api/players?q=&n=&surface=` · `GET /api/players/{name}?vs=`
`GET /api/h2h?a=&b=` · `GET /api/model` (all frozen evidence, one call)
`GET /api/reliability?n_bins=` (binned OOF probs for the diagram)

## Self-improving loop
1. UI `Log model pick` -> sqlite `data/tracker.db` (with model prob + surface)
2. After the match, `POST /api/settle {id, result, closing_fair_odds}`
3. `GET /api/stats` -> win_rate, ROI, avg CLV, calibration bins, suggested min-EV threshold
4. Nightly: `POST /api/learn` -> per-surface Hedge weights + per-surface
   calibration refresh. Poisoned state? `POST /api/rollback {target}` restores
   the newest backup (`weights` | `calibration` | `policy`).

Write endpoints (`/track`, `/settle`, `/learn`, `/rollback`) need
`X-API-Key: $VIBE_API_KEY` once `VIBE_API_KEY` is set in `.env`.

## How the model works (tennis only)
- **Ratings**: surface-blended Elo + H2H + last-10 form/serve/fatigue + decayed
  opponent-adjusted point ratings (Barnett-Clarke style).
- **Markov**: exact point->game->tiebreak->set->match DP (BO3/BO5, TB10 deciders).
- **GBM**: LightGBM on as-of features, time splits only (train<=2022/valid 2023/
  test>=2024), monotone constraints, Brier early-stopping. Gate: test Brier
  < 0.215 and ECE < 0.03 or it ships as REVIEW (ensemble member, not replacement).
- **Ensemble**: per-surface Hedge (eta hard 0.10 / clay 0.07 / grass+carpet 0.05).
  Sleeping signals keep exact share. Weights + calibration hot-reload into the
  running server; every verdict is logged to `data/verdicts.jsonl`.
- **Edge**: computed vs the MARKET-FREE model prob (the full prob saw the
  market at ~0.19 weight — edge-vs-full would dilute every signal).
- **Policy**: contextual bandit (surface, edge, confidence) gates post/pass,
  learns from settled picks. The sim exercises it with pass counterfactuals.
- **Eval**: `python -m backend.sim.season` replays 2024-25 frozen-vs-adaptive
  with a paired test, per-surface + confidence tables, and a paper-trading leg
  (half-Kelly vs market close where present, else the Elo fair line, no vig —
  skill-vs-line, not real profit). `python -m backend.model.ablate` shows which
  signals earn their weight.

## Odds feed notes
- 60s locked file cache; quota guard stops live fetches under 25 remaining
  credits (serves cache, then mock — `/api/health` always says which).
- Fair price = Pinnacle when it agrees with the field, else consensus median
  (flags >12pt disagreement as possibly stale).
